name: upload-queue
purpose: List of files being uploaded, with a Progress Bar per item, status (queued, uploading, done, failed, cancelled), cancel/retry/remove actions, and live announcements. Uploading is transport-agnostic: the consumer supplies upload(file, { signal, onProgress, attempt, id }); the queue adds a concurrency limit, AbortController cancellation, and retries with exponential backoff. It never performs a network request itself.
whenToUse: Uploading files with visible progress and the ability to cancel or retry.
Chunked or resumable uploads (the consumer function loops over chunks and reports progress).
Together with File Upload, or on its own with files from any source.
whenNotToUse: A single small file submitted with the form: submit it natively with File Upload.
Background sync that must survive page reloads: the queue lives in memory.
states: item: queued | uploading | done | failed | cancelled
responsive: Full width. Each row keeps the media (icon or preview), the progress bar (label and description wrap), and 24 px action buttons on one line.
rtl: Logical properties: media at the inline start, actions at the inline end, progress fills from the inline start.
theme: Rows on color-surface with a color-border-strong boundary (color-error-fg when failed); progress uses Progress Bar tones (success on done, error on failed). Forced-colors mode uses CanvasText borders.
security: The queue performs no network access; the consumer function does. File names and messages are rendered with textContent. Rejection reasons are never displayed raw (they may leak server internals): the default is a generic localized message, and errorMessage maps errors to user-facing text. Previews use object URLs in (no script execution), which requires img-src blob: in the CSP; URLs are revoked on removal and destroy.
dataHandling: Files and responses stay in memory for the lifetime of the queue. Nothing is persisted, logged, or transmitted by AbsoluteUI.

budgets.budget: coalesced to one render per animation frame

performance.testedScale: 200 items in the performance test; progress reported for every chunk.

limitations: Cancellation is cooperative: the consumer function must pass signal to fetch/XHR. A function that ignores it keeps its concurrency slot until it settles (the item is shown as cancelled immediately).
Retries restart the whole file; resuming from an offset is the consumer function's job (use attempt and id).
Completion is announced once per batch; individual successes are included in the summary rather than announced one by one.
State is not persisted across reloads.
Manual screen-reader verification (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) is pending.
unsupported: Built-in transports (fetch, XHR, tus, S3 multipart): supply your own function.
Rendering HTML in file names or error messages.
antiPatterns: Showing raw exception or server messages to users.
Ignoring the abort signal in the upload function.
